title: Lane X1 — PostgreSQL Product Materialization — Audit

external_sources_consulted.title: PostgreSQL JSON/JSONB Design and Indexing
external_sources_consulted.key_findings: jsonb_path_ops GIN indexes preferred for containment-heavy queries. Targeted expression indexes for narrow access paths. jsonb over json for all operational storage.

external_sources_consulted.title: PostgreSQL Materialized Views
external_sources_consulted.key_findings: CONCURRENTLY refresh requires UNIQUE index covering all rows. Non-concurrent refresh takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock. WITH NO DATA + REFRESH pattern for deferred population. REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW is the standard mechanism; automatic refresh is not built in.

external_sources_consulted.title: PostgreSQL pg_dump Reference
external_sources_consulted.key_findings: pg_dump supports custom, plain, tar, and directory formats. --no-password, --no-owner, --no-privileges recommended for portable backups. --exclude-table-data can exclude operational snapshot tables.

external_sources_consulted.title: PostgreSQL pg_restore Reference
external_sources_consulted.key_findings: pg_restore with --clean --if-exists --single-transaction provides atomic restore. --list mode allows structural verification without data restore. Supports --no-owner --no-privileges for portable restores.

external_sources_consulted.title: PostgreSQL LISTEN
external_sources_consulted.key_findings: LISTEN registers per-connection, takes effect at COMMIT. Two-phase setup pattern required. Notifications lost on disconnect. Deferred for refresh signalling in this lane.

external_sources_consulted.title: PostgreSQL NOTIFY
external_sources_consulted.key_findings: NOTIFY delivers on COMMIT only. Payload limited to 8000 bytes. Identical channel+payload deduplicated within transaction. Suitable for lightweight signalling, not event authority.

external_sources_consulted.title: PostgreSQL pg_upgrade Reference
external_sources_consulted.key_findings: pg_upgrade performs in-place major version upgrades. Requires both old and new binaries. Supports --check mode for pre-upgrade validation. Deferred for future PostgreSQL version migrations.

external_sources_consulted.title: Psycopg 3 Transaction Management
external_sources_consulted.key_findings: autocommit=True recommended to prevent idle-in-transaction. Transaction blocks via conn.transaction() context manager. SAVEPOINT-based nested transactions. Handle InFailedSqlTransaction by issuing rollback().

migration_list.description: Foundation schema: _schema_version, _migrations, evidence_sources, ingestion_checkpoints, ingestion_receipts, projection_builds, rebuild_receipts, operational_snapshots, notify_channels
Atomic ingestion: UNIQUE constraint on evidence_id, typed conflict detection (digest/schema/path_hash), transactional ingestion with rollback

Repository Estate materialization: registered_repositories, repository_observations, repository_workspace_instances (with UNIQUE (repository_hash, workspace_root_digest)), repository_observation_changes, repository_estate_builds
Investigation Timeline materialization: timeline_events (30 columns, 12 indexes per T4.2 contract), timeline_builds
Publication preview materialization from ledger: publication_preview_receipts, publication_reconstruction, publication_builds
Materialized views for Gridline querying: mv_repository_estate_overview, mv_workspace_status_summary, mv_verified_timeline_summary, mv_publication_preview_summary

materializers.name: RepositoryEstateMaterializer
key_behaviors: Distinguishes logical repository identity from workspace/checkout instances
Instance ID derived from SHA256(repository_hash + workspace_root_digest)
Corrupt observations stored with degraded classification, not discarded
Detects 7 change kinds between consecutive observations
materialize(service) and rebuild(service) support rebuild determinism

materializers.name: TimelineMaterializer
key_behaviors: NOT NULL defaults enforced for 12 columns
Degradation counts computed across 7 categories (verified_canonical, canonical_degraded, corrupt, unsupported, missing, contradictory, stale)
ON CONFLICT (event_id) DO NOTHING for idempotent ingestion
rebuild(service) deletes all rows then re-materializes, checks determinism

materializers.name: PublicationMaterializer
key_behaviors: Deployment readiness always tracked as false (preview-only evidence)
Reconstruction state records total/valid/corrupt rows and corrupt line numbers
Corrupt receipts stored with truthful degraded classification
Evidence source SHA256 computed from sorted receipt IDs
rebuild(ledger) clears and re-materializes all three publication tables

identity_model.title: Repository vs Workspace Identity Model
identity_model.design: Each logical repository has a repository_hash. Each physical workspace instance (clone/worktree) has a distinct workspace_root_digest. The UNIQUE constraint ensures two workspace instances under the same logical repository remain independently observable and never collapse into one row.
identity_model.instance_id: SHA256(repository_hash + workspace_root_digest) truncated to 32 hex chars
proven_by: test_two_workspaces_under_same_repository: inserts two workspace instances for one repo_hash, verifies COUNT = 2
test_independent_dirty_states: verifies distinct dirty counts per workspace instance
test_workspace_state_does_not_collapse: verifies distinct instance IDs and workspace_root_digests
integrity_rules: Each workspace instance tracks its own head_sha, branch, is_detached state
Dirty counts (modified, staged, untracked, deleted, conflicted) are per-instance
Partial index on (repository_hash) WHERE total_dirty > 0 for dirty-workspace queries

content_light.title: Content-Light Guarantees
guarantees: All tables store SHA256 digests only — no raw file contents
No raw paths stored: workspace_root_digest is a salted SHA256, not a raw filesystem path
No raw prompts or model outputs anywhere in PostgreSQL tables
No API keys, tokens, credentials, or environment variable values
Evidence sources stored by evidence_id (content-hash-derived), evidence_kind, evidence_sha256 — never raw payload
Backup receipts reference backup_sha256 and backup_size_bytes — never raw backup contents
PostgresBackupService uses --no-password flag; passwords never stored in db or receipts
clear_projection_data preserves _schema_version and _migrations (authority records) — everything else is disposable

backup_restore.title: Backup/Restore Boundary
backup_restore.backup_method: pg_dump (custom, plain, tar, or directory format)
backup_restore.verification: pg_restore --list for structural validation without data restore
content_light_receipts: BackupReceipt: receipt_id, backup_method, database_name, schema_name, format, backup_sha256, backup_size_bytes, table_count, migration_version, secrets_excluded, backed_up_at, verified
RestoreReceipt: receipt_id, backup_sha256, restore_method, restored_at, tables_restored, rows_restored, migration_version_restored, canonical_equivalence_verified, verification_method, errors
backup_restore.canonical_equivalence: Post-restore verification checks _schema_version and _migrations records exist — does not replace canonical evidence restoration

rebuild_determinism.title: Rebuild Determinism
rebuild_determinism.clear_projection_data: Deletes from 15 tables: timeline_builds, timeline_events, repository_estate_builds, repository_observation_changes, repository_observations, repository_workspace_instances, registered_repositories, publication_builds, publication_preview_receipts, publication_reconstruction, rebuild_receipts, projection_builds, ingestion_receipts, ingestion_checkpoints, evidence_sources
rebuild_determinism.preserves: _schema_version, _migrations, notify_channels, materialized views (materialized views are derived from operational tables and can be refreshed independently)
determinism_contract: Each domain materializer has rebuild(service_or_ledger) method
Rebuild counts rows_before, clears tables, re-materializes, counts rows_after
RebuildReceipt records rows_before, rows_after, and deterministic flag (rows_before == rows_after)

authority_separation.title: Canonical Authority Separation
authority_separation.principle: PostgreSQL is explicitly a disposable read-side projection. Canonical evidence ledgers (JSONL, append-only) remain the sole authority for governed transitions.
evidence: Every PostgreSQL domain table is preceded by docstrings declaring 'PostgreSQL is a disposable read-side projection'
EvidenceSource model stores only evidence_id, evidence_kind, evidence_sha256, source_ledger_path_hash — never raw payload
clear_projection_data drops all domain rows while preserving schema authority tables
RebuildReceipt validates deterministic reconstruction from canonical evidence
BackupReceipt.restoreReceipt explicitly declares canonical equivalence verification is separate from data restoration

test_evidence.substrate_note: All tests run against real PostgreSQL 17.10 via disposable test databases. No SQLite, no in-memory substitute, no test doubles for database operations.
